reviews.title: Structured: Technische Probleme mit Benachrichtigungen nach Deinstallation
reviews.text:
Nach der Deinstallation von Structured unter macOS wurden weiterhin geplante Benachrichtigungen angezeigt, obwohl die Anwendung nicht mehr installiert war.
Die Herkunft dieser Mitteilungen war zunächst nicht erkennbar. Erst eine technische Untersuchung der macOS-Mitteilungsdatenbank mittels Terminal und SQLite brachte Klarheit:
App-Kennung: com.leomehlig.today (Structured)
29 gespeicherte Benachrichtigungseinträge ohne Zustellzeitpunkt.
Benachrichtigungen erschienen weiterhin nach der ursprünglichen Deinstallation.
Die Bereinigung erforderte eine erneute Installation von Structured und die manuelle Deaktivierung der Mitteilungen sowohl innerhalb der App als auch in den macOS-Systemeinstellungen.
Erst danach waren die 29 Einträge aus der Datenbank verschwunden.
Auch nach erneuter Deinstallation und Neustart blieb die App-Registrierung in der macOS-Datenbank bestehen.
Ob die Ursache in Structured, der Verwaltung geplanter Benachrichtigungen durch macOS oder deren Zusammenspiel liegt, lässt sich nicht abschließend feststellen.
Kritisch ist aus Anwendersicht, dass Benachrichtigungen nach der Deinstallation weiterhin auftraten und zur Behebung technische Eingriffe beziehungsweise eine erneute Installation erforderlich waren.
Von einer Organisations-App erwarte ich, dass geplante Benachrichtigungen zuverlässig verwaltet und beim Entfernen der Anwendung sauber beendet werden.
Fazit: Erheblicher technischer und zeitlicher Aufwand zur Beseitigung unerwünschter Benachrichtigungen. Für

reviews.title: Paid for Lifetime, Disappointed by Missing Two-Way Calendar Sync
reviews.text:
Structured is a great app in many respects, and I paid for the lifetime subscription. However, the lack of two-way calendar sync is a major limitation for me. I need changes made in the app to update my calendar and vice versa.

That’s why I use the lifetime version of Planny, another German app, instead. For a paid planning app, seamless two-way calendar integration is something I consider essential. Disappointing that Structured still doesn’t offer it.

I’m a student looking to use an app for tracking daily class schedules and blocking out study time, but the fact that the ability to repeat events is locked behind the pro version disappoints me greatly. I know that it’s probably a smaller team independently making the app but making repeated events paywalled makes this app useless for students that don’t want to be burdened with yet another subscription fee or pay a whopping $100 one-time payment. The other option is to tediously manually enter in repeating events every day, but who would bother to do that every single day? I have ADHD and was looking for an app to help manage my time and scheduling and having to input every repeating event manually is not feasible for me. Unfortunate since I thought this might actually be an app that could help, but I guess I have to go back to searching.

reviews.title: Important features missing
reviews.text:
I thought I had finally found my perfect task management app, but sadly not.  

Unfortunately there is no facility to allocate a priority to tasks.  A key part of time management is capturing the tasks that need doing and being able to prioritise them BEFORE you schedule them in your day.  This app jumps straight into scheduling without giving a system for choosing which tasks are actually needed.   In an ideal world you should be able to set up a system for how you prioritise your tasks (there are a variety of different ways), and view your tasks in a priority view THEN schedule. Apps like tick tick or todoist do this very well but don’t have the visual appeal of Structured.  I would totally switch if the task capturing and prioritisation side of Structured was improved.

reviews.title: Day 2 of my trial and I’m NOT subscribing when it ends
reviews.text:
I really wanted to like Structured because it advertises itself as being especially helpful for people with ADHD. Unfortunately, my experience during the trial was the opposite.

The AI was the main reason I considered paying for the app, but it ended up creating more work instead of saving me time. I would ask it to schedule tasks, then have to go back and manually fix the schedule. When I asked it to move a multi-step outing (such as a library trip with walking there, signing up for library cards, browsing, and walking home), it only moved one task and left the others behind. That completely broke the plan and forced me to reorganize everything myself.

Recurring tasks were another major frustration. When I tried to delete a recurring task, I wasn’t given the expected options to delete just one occurrence, all future occurrences, or the entire series. Instead, I had to edit the recurrence before I could finally remove it. That’s confusing and unnecessarily time-consuming.

Importing Apple Reminders was another disappointing experience. I have well-organized reminder lists with headings, tasks, and subtasks. Structured completely flattened everything during the import, splitting headings, tasks, and subtasks into individual inbox items. Instead of preserving the organization, it created a cluttered mess.

reviews.text:
I'm a paying annual subscriber and genuinely like what Structured is trying to do. The timeline view is thoughtful and the sync across devices works well, when the app is actually running.

The problem is that on macOS the app freezes regularly and stops responding entirely. The only fix is a Force Quit. This has happened often enough that I no longer trust the app to be open when I need it. For a daily planner, that's a serious reliability issue.

I'd also encourage the developer to revisit what data is being sent to third-party services:
posthog.com
8-lives-cat.io
revenuecat.com
configcat.com
sentry.io

As a paying customer I was surprised to find the app contacts analytics platforms in the background,the kind of behavioural tracking that makes sense for a free app trying to convert users, less so for an annual subscription.

I want to keep using Structured. But the freezing needs to be fixed, and paying users deserve transparency about what the app is doing in the background.

reviews.title: Useful. However Causes Excess Battery Drain
reviews.text: Honestly, this is a really good application. I really love the UI and it’s pretty easy to use. I especially love how there is a Web version which allows me to use it for my day to day planning at work. Overall it’s intuitive and very good for people who like to stay organized and use daily planners. The one caveat with this application and the only reason I didn’t give it 5 stars (and also the reason I am on the fence about subscribing for it) is the battery drain on this app. It appears that this application has NOT been optimized AT ALL for battery efficiency. I am on the iPhone 17 Pro Max, my battery is fantastic. That said - THIS APP DRAINS IT. After several days of usage, I’ve been able to determine it drains about 0.36% of battery per minute. Which I mean, doesn’t seem like much at first glance. But when you run the math on it, that means just using this app for about 25ish minutes a day will drain 10% of your battery.. That’s a lot for a todo/daily planner application. The first day I got the app and I set up my schedule and all my repeating tasks, I used the app for about 1 hour and 5 minutes of screen on time, that resulted in 25% battery usage. To be blunt, that’s horrendously poor optimization. Just for perspective, highly resource intensive applications such as BlackMagic Camera when filming in 60 FPS at 4K use the EXACT SAME amount of battery as this application per minute. reviews.text:
I love this app, but unable to use on my iPhone. More specifically, here is more context to help you hopefully make an adjustment if you can! 
My context: 
- iPhone15 Pro Max. 
- IOS 26
- Coincidently (maybe?) my other app (NextThere) has the exact same issue (see issue below)
- I click on the app (Structured), the Structured logo (the pink tick) appears in the centre of my screen surrounded by blackness for 1 second then the app crashes. If I click on the app after it crashes the same thing happens, the logo appears then the app crashes. Always the same.
- I CAN use the app on my MacBook air (without any problem), but my app (on my iPhone) is what I use all the time. I almost never use Structured on my MacBook Air. 

I use this app so much. Has helped with my ADHD diagnoses.  If you need anymore info please let me know?! Thanks!

reviews.title: Gute iOS-/Web-App, sehr schlechte macOS App
reviews.text: Nicht falsch verstehen, ich mochte Structured schon vor Jahren. Jetzt wollte ich es wieder benutzen und mir die Lifetime-Version holen, vor allem da es mittlerweile eine macOS-Version gibt und man über die Cloud synchroneren kann. Doch leider bin ich sehr ernüchtert. Die gesamte Bedienung hinkt der Web-App sehr hinterher, es ist richtig lästig zu verwenden. Viele Ansichtsmodi im Web, nur eine einzige in der macOS App, egal wie groß man das Fenster zieht. Das wechseln zwischen Tagen ist nicht möglich, sondern nur zwischen Wochen. Um an einem Sonntag auf morgen zu kommen, müsste man also mehrere Klicks durchführen (nächste Woche, Montag anklicken). Keine Anzeige des Wochentages, dadurch denkt man bei Klick auf den Pfeil rechts, man sehe in der *Tagesansicht* den nächsten Tag. Man sieht an einem Freitag aber den nächsten Freitag und plant völlig falsch, weil man das nicht direkt versteht. Verschieben der Aufgaben zwischen den Tagen ist die absolute Krätze: Aufmachen, Kalender anklicken, Tag suchen, komplett überladen werden von hunderten Icons und trotzdem nicht wissen wohin man will, Ansicht wieder verlassen, superaufwändig den gewünschten Zieltag suchen, dann wieder zurückgehen, Termin anklicken und dann die Zeit mit Dutzenden !!! Klicks einstellen. Warum man sich dazu entschieden hat, fancy UI Bedienelemente vom iPhone auf den Mac zu übernehmen weiß auch kein Mensch. Ich kann von mir aus durch Zeiten scrollen, aber ich will sie auch eingeben können ohne dass ich dafür in ein
